match.reason: The closest bank point, Map conventions, covers all six parts of a map and gives only a brief note on scale, with no ratio, line or word scales and no compass points, so it is broader than this point and no bank point teaches map scale and direction as this card does.

draft.title: Map scale and direction
card: Scale shows how a distance on a map relates to the real distance on the ground. It can be a ratio, a line scale or words.
A ratio of 1:50 000 means 1 unit on the map is 50 000 of the same unit on the ground. So 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm, or 500 m, in real life.
A north arrow points to north on the map. The compass points are north, east, south and west, with north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west between them.
To find a real distance, measure the map distance, then use the scale to change it. To give a direction, say which compass point one place is from another.
draft.remember: Scale turns map distance into real distance. The north arrow and compass points give direction.

a.q: A map has a scale of 1:50 000. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
a.why: 1 cm on the map is 500 m on the ground, so 4 cm is 4 × 500 m = 2000 m, or 2 km. 200 m is tempting, but it comes from reading 1 cm as 50 m.
a.clue: First work out what 1 cm stands for in metres.

b.q: Ravi's map of Bendigo has a scale of 1:25 000. The library is 6 cm north-east of the station on the map. Which is true?
opts: It is 1.5 km from the station, to the north-east
It is 1.5 km from the station, to the south-west
It is 15 km from the station, to the north-east
It is 150 m from the station, to the north-east
b.why: 1 cm is 25 000 cm, which is 250 m, so 6 cm is 1500 m, or 1.5 km. The library is north-east of the station, so it is not south-west. The option of 15 km mistakes the distance by a factor of ten.
b.clue: Find what 1 cm stands for, then say which place the direction starts from.

b.best: It is 1.5 km from the station, to the north-east
